summary: Implemented the cross-LAN firewall requirement with an Ansible playbook (cross-lan-firewall.yml + inventory.ini, staged on node4/control_node at /root/ansible-cross-lan-firewall/). It statically addresses node2's lan-a NIC (10.50.10.11/24) and node3's lan-b NIC (10.50.20.12/24) with a specific route to the peer subnet via node1, opens node3's local firewalld only for tcp/5432 from the lan-a CIDR, and configures VyOS (node1) with eth1=10.50.10.254/24, eth2=10.50.20.254/24 and a forward-filter firewall (accept established/related, accept tcp/5432 from eth1->eth2, default-action drop). Verified node2->node3:5432 succeeds while ICMP, other ports, and the reverse direction are all blocked. The tricky part: VyOS's non-interactive config-session setup (cli-shell-api setupSession) silently fails when invoked directly as the 'vyos' user over SSH; the fix was to escalate via the vyos user's passwordless sudo (become: true/sudo) so the VyOS config script runs as root, which reliably creates the config session. All 4 managed nodes were then restarted one at a time, each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of networking/firewall/tooling state, and the playbook was re-run successfully from node4 after its own reboot to prove Ansible-driven recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router with eth0(mgmt)/eth1/eth2, node2/node3=RHEL9 with enp1s0(mgmt)/enp8s0(lan), node4=Ubuntu ansible-controller (control_node)
Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user)/node2/node3 (root) using the cluster keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY)
Determined via ping tests that node1 eth1 faces node2 (lan-a) and eth2 faces node3 (lan-b)
Wrote Ansible inventory.ini and cross-lan-firewall.yml (3 plays: address node2, address node3 + firewalld rich-rule, configure VyOS firewall on node1) and staged them on node4

Diagnosed a VyOS bug where cli-shell-api setupSession fails when 'configure' is invoked as the vyos user over plain SSH (first-session-creation issue), and fixed it by adding become:true/become_method:sudo to the VyOS task so it runs as root via vyos's passwordless sudo
Ran the playbook end-to-end twice (initial + idempotent re-run) and verified idempotency (firewalld task skips when rule already present)
Verified node2->node3:5432 succeeds, node2->node3:8080 and ICMP are blocked, and node3->node2:5432 (reverse direction) is blocked

Captured boot_id + service/network health baselines on all 4 nodes, restarted each one at a time via native `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified full recovery of network config, firewalld rules, VyOS firewall config, and Ansible tooling (including re-running the playbook successfully from node4 after its own reboot)

evidence.requirement: Ansible playbook implements node2->node3:5432 allow with default reject between lan-a/lan-b
evidence.summary: Playbook run (initial + idempotent re-run) shows node1/node2/node3 all 'ok', and node1 nftables forward-filter chain shows accept established/related, accept tcp/5432 eth1->eth2, default drop

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on tcp/5432
evidence.summary: Python socket connect from node2 to 10.50.20.12:5432 succeeds and receives 'ok' both right after playbook run and after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: All other lan-a<->lan-b traffic is rejected (other ports, ICMP, reverse direction)
evidence.summary: node2->node3:8080 times out, ICMP ping node2->node3 100% loss, and node3->node2:5432 (wrong direction) times out

evidence.requirement: VyOS config (addresses + firewall) persists in config.boot / nftables
evidence.summary: Post-reboot config.boot shows eth1/eth2 addresses and firewall rules intact; nftables chain matches the intended ruleset

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 4098161f...->98d4541d... after native `reboot`; post-restart config.boot and live connectivity test both confirm full recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id f1afbc7f...->00399174... after reboot; enp8s0 static address/route and systemctl is-system-running=running confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id b634b53f...->f13b88a4... after reboot; enp8s0 address/route, firewalld rich-rule, and firewalld active state confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 416c5cf5...->8d76d172... after reboot; ansible-playbook files, cluster SSH key, and ansible binary all intact, and a full playbook re-run against node1/node2/node3 succeeds post-reboot
